Let's denote the indefinite integral by $I=\int \frac{{ln}^{9}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x.$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{9}⁡x & \,⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{9{ln}^{8}⁡x}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4x} & \,⇒\,v=\int \frac{1}{4x}\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int \frac{{ln}^{9}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({ln}^{9}⁡x)(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4})(\frac{9{ln}^{8}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{ln}^{10}⁡x}{4}-9\int \frac{{ln}^{9}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{ln}^{10}⁡x}{4}-9I.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for $I.$ We can ignore the constant of integration in this case, because it is insignificant for further evaluation of the definite integral.

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\frac{{ln}^{10}⁡x}{4}-9I \\ 10I & =\frac{{ln}^{10}⁡x}{4} \\ I & =\frac{{ln}^{10}⁡x}{40}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate our definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}\frac{{ln}^{9}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{40}({ln}^{10}⁡x){|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{1}{40}({ln}^{10}⁡(e)-{ln}^{10}⁡(1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{40}\end{aligned}
$$
